We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Research the official free-tier limits of the GitHub Actions service for public and private repositories (minutes, storage, concurrency). Cite the GitHub documentation page you used.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official GitHub documentation, here are the free-tier limits for GitHub Actions regarding minutes, storage, and concurrency for both public and private repositories.

### Public Repositories
For public repositories, the use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited in terms of minutes and basic concurrency, though specific job execution time limits still apply.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free: ... In public repositories" | CLAIM: Standard GitHub-hosted runner usage is free for public repositories.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-where-workflows-run/choose-the-runner-for-a-job#standard-github-hosted-runners-for-public-repositories | QUOTE: "Use of the standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited on public repositories." | CLAIM: There is no minute limit for standard runners in public repositories.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each job in a workflow can run for up to 6 hours of execution time. If a job reaches this limit, the job is terminated and fails." | CLAIM: Even in public repositories, individual jobs on GitHub-hosted runners are limited to 6 hours of execution time.

### Private Repositories (Free Tier Plans)
For private repositories, free-tier accounts (GitHub Free, GitHub Free for organizations) receive a specific monthly quota of minutes and storage. Usage beyond these quotas is billed.

**Minutes and Storage Quotas:**

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: GitHub Free plan includes 2,000 minutes per month, 500 MB artifact storage, and 10 GB cache storage.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| GitHub Free for organizations | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: GitHub Free for organizations plan includes 2,000 minutes per month, 500 MB artifact storage, and 10 GB cache storage.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "Your free minutes reset to the full amount at the start of each billing cycle." | CLAIM: Minute quotas reset monthly.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "Storage charges accumulate throughout the month based on hourly usage. Your accrued storage charges reset to zero at the start of each billing cycle." | CLAIM: Storage limits are soft caps that incur billing if exceeded, rather than hard stops, and reset monthly.

**Concurrency Limits for Private Repositories (Free Plan):**

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "| Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Free | 20 | 5 | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Free plan allows 20 total concurrent jobs and a maximum of 5 concurrent macOS jobs on standard GitHub-hosted runners.

### General Limits (Applies to Both Public and Private)
Regardless of the repository type or plan, certain operational limits apply to ensure system stability.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each repository is limited to events triggering a workflow run. ... 1500 events / 10 seconds / repository" | CLAIM: There is a rate limit of 1,500 workflow trigger events per 10 seconds per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "When the limit is reached, the workflow runs that were supposed to be triggered by the webhook events will be blocked and will not be queued. ... 500 workflow runs / 10 seconds" | CLAIM: A maximum of 500 workflow runs can be queued per 10 seconds.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each repository is limited to 200 cache entry uploads per minute." | CLAIM: Cache uploads are limited to 200 per minute per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each repository is limited to 1500 cache entry downloads per minute." | CLAIM: Cache downloads are limited to 1,500 per minute per repository.

### Uncertain / Not Found
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Specific concurrency limits (number of parallel jobs) for public repositories are not explicitly quantified in the provided tables, which primarily list limits for paid plans (Free, Pro, Team, Enterprise). The text states usage is "unlimited" for public repos regarding minutes, but does not provide a specific number for max concurrent jobs for public repos, implying it may be subject to general system limits or fair use policies not detailed in the static tables.
